transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-24
Start time (UTC): 16:00
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Carlos Ruiz (Orchid AI - Head of Search), Aisha Khan (Orchid AI - ML Engineer), Tom Sanders (Orchid AI - CTO)

Summary:
- Discovery focused on embeddings + reranking workflows, vector DB choices, throughput/QPS, dimensionality, and hybrid search (lexical + vector).
- Customer evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for latency/cost and data residency; strong security requirements (SOC2, KMS, VPC).
- Agreed next steps: pricing sheet, security docs, pilot benchmark, technical deep dive on FAISS/hybrid config.

Topics:
- Current stack and pain points
- Vector DB + embeddings dims (512 vs 1536)
- Reranking flow (embedding + cross-encoder rerank) and throughput implications
- Hybrid search (BM25 + ANN) and recall/latency tradeoffs
- Deployment: hosted vs dedicated vs private (VPC/on-prem)
- Security & compliance: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros - i'm jordan with redwood, ae on the account. maya, our se, will cover the technical bits.
[00:15] Carlos Ruiz: hey, carlos here. i'll kick off - head of search at orchid. we run a customer support search and prod knowledge base retrieval.
[00:25] Aisha Khan: aisha, ml eng. we own indexing and reranking pipelines.
[00:30] Tom Sanders: tom, cto. i'll be mostly listening for infra/security questions.
[00:36] Maya Chen: thanks. goal for today is to understand your current stack, qps/latency needs, and where embeddings+rerank fit. we'll talk options: hosted, dedicated, private.
[00:50] Carlos: cool. quick background - we ingest FAQs, support transcripts, internal docs. currently using TF-IDF + a small dense-vector system (we built a in-house faiss-ish solution). running about 200 qps peak, but search latency target is sub-200ms P95 for the initial recall stage. rerank uses a cross-encoder model that is more expensive and runs for top-20 candidates.
[01:12] Jordan: okay, good context. curious - what embedding model/dimensionality are you using today?
[01:20] Aisha: right now embeddings are 768 dims, custom trained on our data. looking at migrating to off-the-shelf 1536 dim models for quality, but worried about index size and throughput.
[01:33] Maya: that's a common tradeoff. higher dims = better semantic separation typically but bigger indexes and slower ANN search. for redwood hosted we recommend profiling both 768 and 1536 with your dataset. we have quantized variants and can serve 1536 with moderate perf hit; dedicated hosts with more RAM/GPU help.
[01:55] Carlos: when you say quantized variants - do you support int8 or 4-bit for embeddings? how does that affect cosine similarity / KNN recall?
[02:05] Maya: we have several quantization profiles. for embeddings we often see minimal recall loss with 8-bit quantization on vectors, but 4-bit is trickier. we can run A/B on your dataset. note: some vector DBs don't support lower-bit natively; we put a small post-processing step.
[02:25] Tom: on vector DBs - we're evaluating pinecone and milvus. curious if redwood has recommended integrations or if you run your own index?
[02:35] Jordan: Redwood's hosted flow can integrate with external vector DBs for storage and ANN (we've connectors for Pinecone/Weaviate/Milvus). we also offer an integrated index option for hosted customers to reduce network hops. in dedicated/private deployments teams often bring Milvus or self-hosted FAISS for full control.
[02:56] Aisha: network hops are a big concern for us if embeddings are served by redwood but stored externally. that round-trip could kill p95.
[03:05] Maya: agreed - if you care about single-digit ms we're usually recommending colocated index or dedicated deployment where the embedding server and ANN backend are on the same VPC or cluster. for hosted, we can colocate in the same region but there is still additional network path.
[03:20] [03:20] Carlos: our expected traffic pattern is spiky: nightly batch indexing, daytime support peaks. around 200 qps average, 500 qps burst. rerank QPS lower but heavy CPU/GPU for cross-encoder.
[03:36] Maya: good to know. for throughput questions - are you batching queries? do you plan to do online per-request embeddings or precompute?
[03:45] Aisha: we precompute for documents; end-user queries are online embeddings, so we need low-latency per-query embed + ANN recall + rerank pipeline.
[03:56] Jordan: so end-to-end latency budget?
[04:00] Carlos: ideally search recall + rerank under 400ms for interactive support. rerank can be async in some flows but for chat it's inline.
[04:10] Maya: for inline cross-encoder rerank, we typically recommend two approaches: 1) smaller cross-encoder for top-50 with CPU-based runners (cheaper) or 2) GPU-based dedicated nodes for sub-200ms rerank. dedicated GPUs give predictable tail latencies.
[04:28] Aisha: cost is material - GPU rerank for all queries could blow up. we might use hybrid: cheap lexical/BM25 + ANN for recall, then GPU rerank only for high-value queries or longer sessions.
[04:43] Jordan: that's our Optimize philosophy - we provide routing policies and quality/cost controls to route to cheaper variants or fallbacks on overload. you can set SLO rules to only GPU rerank above certain confidence or user tiers.
[04:58] Tom: security - we operate in EU, data residency required. SOC2 is must. also need KMS integration and audit logs for access to customer data.
[05:09] Maya: we support SOC2-compliant hosted regions, dedicated in-customer VPCs, and private on-prem installs. KMS/HSM integrations are available for private deployments; for hosted we integrate with managed KMS and provide customer-managed keys in Dedicated/Private. audit logs and per-request traces are in the console. we'll share the SOC2 report and integration guide.
[05:29] Carlos: perfect. what's your typical onboarding for a pilot? we want to run a benchmark with our dataset and QPS profile.
[05:37] Jordan: typical: 2-week pilot where we ingest your sample data, index it (we'll test dims 768 & 1536), run search/recall benchmarks, and measure end-to-end latency at your target QPS. we can run hosted pilot or spin up a dedicated sandbox.
[05:52] Aisha: for the pilot, we need to test hybrid search - how do you support BM25 + ANN?
[05:58] Maya: our reranking pipeline supports pre-filtering with BM25 or metadata filters, then ANN recall and optional cross-encoder rerank. Hybrid search is configured in the route: you can do BM25 top-k (k=100) then ANN top-200 merge, or ANN-first with lexical boost. tuneable.
[06:18] Carlos: do you have benchmarks on index size & memory for 1536 dims? approximations?
[06:24] Maya: approximate numbers: raw float32 vectors at 1536 dims ~6KB per vector; with ivf+hnsw+pq/quantization we can reduce to ~0.5-1KB per vector depending on PQ settings. again dataset dependent. we can also use product quantization to drop memory.
[06:40] Tom: what about disk vs memory tradeoffs? we want to keep hot shards in memory for latency, colder shards on SSD.
[06:47] Maya: yep - typical pattern: hot partition in RAM-backed ANN, cold partitions on NVMe with async fallback. dedicated deployment allows more memory per shard. hosted can offer larger instance types for hot sets.
[06:59] [06:59] Carlos: any guidance on dimensionality choice? 768 vs 1536 - what should we weigh?
[07:06] Maya: key is quality uplift vs index cost. run offline evals (MRR, nDCG) on your labeled pairs. if 1536 gives small incremental gains, 768 quantized may be better. if semantic nuance is critical (long docs, subtle intents), 1536 often helps. also model type matters - some models are more efficient at 768.
[07:27] Aisha: we do have a small labeled set for eval, we'll share.
[07:31] Jordan: perfect. another point - rerank models: cross-encoders are expensive. you can use two-stage: cheap bi-encoder for initial rerank then cross-encoder for final top-10. that balances cost.
[07:45] Maya: also caching prefix queries and user session KV caching can dramatically reduce embedding calls for common queries. Redwood supports prefix/KV caching in the runtime.
[07:56] Carlos: interesting. can we control cache TTL and invalidation?
[08:01] Maya: yes - configurable per-route. you can tie cache keys to semantic hash + user scope.
[08:08] Tom: what SLAs do you offer on hosted?
[08:11] Jordan: hosted has best-effort with uptime metrics, dedicated has an SLA (we can share numbers in the pricing sheet). private deployments come with enterprise support contracts.
[08:21] [08:21] Aisha: any examples of customers running similar stacks?
[08:24] Maya: several enterprise customers run hybrid BM25 + ANN with dedicated GPUs for rerank; we have a case where switching to lower-dim quantized embeddings reduced infra cost by 40% with minimal quality loss.
[08:37] Carlos: great. about integration work - how invasive is it to change our pipeline?
[08:41] Jordan: typical integration includes: API keys, pushing embeddings (or calling hosted embed endpoint), configuring index / vector DB, and wiring rerank calls. for dedicated/private we assist with VPC peering, Terraform modules, and deployment runbook.
[08:58] Maya: for on-prem we provide a private control plane and an appliance package; the initial install needs network and KMS setup.
[09:07] Aisha: do you offer prebuilt connectors to our logging stack (elk) for audit logs?
[09:12] Maya: yes - audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM via syslog/S3 or webhook integrations.
[09:18] Carlos: pricing - high-level, how do you charge for embeddings vs rerank GPU time?
[09:22] Jordan: hosted pricing is usage-based: per-embedding token/unit, per-rerank GPU-second or per-inference. dedicated is reserved capacity with commit and overage. we'll share a detailed hosted vs dedicated pricing sheet.
[09:36] Tom: for dedicated landings, what's lead time?
[09:39] Jordan: provisioning dedicated pools is usually 2-4 weeks depending on capacity; private on-prem timelines vary with procurement.
[09:46] Carlos: compliance question - do you support SAML SSO and RBAC for console access?
[09:50] Maya: yes, SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC roles available. audit trails for all admin operations.
[09:58] Aisha: any gotchas with vector DB migration? we have a legacy FAISS store with custom sharding.
[10:05] Maya: migration is a common pain point. we typically recommend a staged approach: 1) export vectors, 2) run indexing in parallel, 3) run A/B traffic split. Redwood tooling can help with bulk ingestion and rollout.
[10:17] Carlos: on hybrid search - any recommended ANN algos? hnsw vs ivf-pq?
[10:22] Maya: HNSW is great for recall and lower latency at cost of memory; IVF+PQ is compact and good for very large corpora but needs tuning. many teams use HNSW for hot partitions and IVF+PQ for cold.
[10:36] [10:36] Jordan: shall we capture the pilot scope? idea: two-week hosted pilot, run both 768 and 1536 embeddings, measure recall & latency at target QPS, test hybrid config, and provide cost estimates.
[10:50] Tom: sounds good. would we be able to try a dedicated sandbox for the pilot to measure tail latencies?
[10:56] Maya: yes - we can spin up a short-lived dedicated sandbox (adds time to provisioning but gives realistic tail latencies).
[11:05] Carlos: for the pilot dataset - we'll provide a 5-10k doc sample and labeled queries.
[11:12] Aisha: we'll also provide expected QPS traces.
[11:16] Jordan: great. we'll follow up with a pilot plan, pricing, and security docs.
[11:22] [11:22] Carlos: quick question - are there any hard limits on embedding dimensionality in hosted?
[11:27] Maya: not hard limits, but practical concerns: higher dims mean more memory and CPU for indexing. we support up to 4096 dims but recommend validating.
[11:36] Tom: if we need private deployment for EU-only residency, are there extra costs for the private control plane?
[11:41] Jordan: yes, private includes platform licensing and support fees; we'll include ballpark numbers in the pricing sheet.
[11:49] Maya: and for KMS, HSM integrations there's an additional services cost to configure in private/dedicated setups.
[11:58] Carlos: okay wrapping up - any other blockers?
[12:02] Aisha: none right now, just waiting on pilot contract and SOC2.
[12:06] Jordan: action items recap - we'll send pricing + pilot contract (Jordan), security docs (Maya), you (Aisha) will share dataset and QPS traces.
[12:19] Tom: sounds good. one more - do you have examples of hybrid search configs we can reuse?
[12:24] Maya: yes, sending a short doc and a benchmark spreadsheet link after the call.
[12:30] Jordan: ok thanks everyone. we'll follow up by end of week.
